canonical_data: per-execution task graphs, checkpoints, task and model-call traces in PostgreSQL when persistence is enabled, with execution-scoped folders of artifacts and large tool responses as Parquet files on disk or S3-compatible storage
current_repo_note: No licence file has ever existed in this repository and the package manifest declares none; the readme's closing section says Apache 2.0 and links a LICENSE file that is not served, so that sentence is the only artifact asserting terms. The last commit was on 2026-02-16.
strengths: The recursion is machinery rather than prose: an engine builds a task dependency graph, runs ready subtasks in parallel, and a checkpoint manager snapshots the graph so a run can be resumed or partly recovered
Database tables record executions, checkpoints, task traces, model calls, tool invocations and circuit-breaker state, so a run can be inspected after the fact
Atomizer, planner, executor, aggregator and verifier are separate configurable modules, with MCP toolkits, a web search toolkit, a terminal toolkit over tmux and an E2B sandbox toolkit
weaknesses: No licence file exists and the manifest declares none, so redistribution terms rest on one readme sentence
The package is version 0.1.0 and labelled beta in its own title, and the last commit was in February 2026
No approval or confirmation step was found around the terminal and code-execution toolkits, so human control is limited to configuration and stopping a run
The benchmark results in the readme are images of the maintainers' own search configuration, not reproducible figures in the repository
why_it_matters: A clear reference for recursive plan-and-aggregate agent execution with a real task graph, checkpoints and traces, held back by the absence of any licence grant.
